paragraphs.text: Magic Beyond Boosters are booster packs specific to Universes Beyond releases. They were featured with Assassin's Creed in 2024 as a variation on the earlier Epilogue Booster .

Beyond Boosters are 7-card Booster packs that contain five "slots" (or card options) — three cards are uncommon cards, one is a land card that has a chance to be replaced with a scene card, one is a rare or mythic rare , one card is a foil "wildcard" that can be of any rarity, and one card is a Booster Fun variant that can be of any rarity. Beyond Boosters also include one non- Magic card, with a chance for that to be either a token or an ad card . At seven cards in total, Beyond Boosters are not designed to be drafted .

Each Beyond Booster is supposed to "tell a story". For Assassin's Creed , you usually get an Assassin first. Then, it features different components from the game— a location, a target for your Assassin, an action, an Equipment, etc. Note that none of the above components are guaranteed to be in any one particular booster, but the as-fan is high enough that many, especially the Assassins, should appear in most boosters.
Beyond Boosters are designed specifically for 60 card formats (i.e. Modern ) with a goal being to "provide evergreen staples". A booster box of Beyond Boosters contains 24 packs.
Beyond Boosters were not made available on Magic Online .
Beyond Boosters were not available on Magic: The Gathering Arena .

Beyond boosters were designed to solve a set structure issue with Assassin's Creed , where the set was not a good fit for a Commander deck release because it lacked enough factions to build around but was also not a good fit for a full tentpole release. The lack of options forced Wizards of the Coast to examine alternate methods of getting cards into players hands. The middle ground was to use and modify the then unreleased Epilogue booster.

Beyond Boosters had already been designed prior to the release of March of the Machine: The Aftermath , with Wizards of the Coast being internally happy using the Epilogue-style product structure. The overwhelmingly negative reception to March of the Machine: The Aftermath caused Wizards to redesign the structure of Beyond boosters, minimizing the common complaints about card repetition and price. The booster was increased to seven cards in size, up from five, while booster boxes were reduced in size to 24 packs. These changes, coupled with the larger set size for Assassin's Creed , were aimed at reducing the number of duplicate uncommons players would open across a booster box. According to the designers, the new structure allowed for players to open more "cool cards", with an increase in the number of potential rares and mythics going to four, up from three. The price of Beyond booster packs was also said to be changed in response to player complaints about the expense of March of the Machine: The Aftermath boosters, but in fact the price went up instead of down.

Beyond Boosters were considered a failure by Wizards of the Coast . Assassin’s Creed sold well because the attraction of the property, but market research showed that the Beyond Booster itself - similar to the Epilogue Booster - was not well liked. With the shift to Standard legal Universes Beyond sets in 2025 , this diminished the possibility of another set with Beyond Boosters in the future.
The set being undraftable was conceived as a negative. As of 2025, all randomized booster releases would have a limited play component (which includes drafting as a big element).

The design of Marvel's Spider-Man initially started out as 100 card set without commons, similar to Assassin’s Creed . As response to the feedback, the set was made bigger. In addition, the Pick-Two Draft was developed to accommodate these smaller sets.
